Venus Williams. An American tennis champion who won seven Grand Slam singles titles and pioneered women's tennis in the modern era alongside her sister Serena. Her powerful serve and aggressive game revolutionized women's tennis, and her dominance in the 1990s and 2000s made her an icon of athleticism and grace. She won one Australian Open, two French Opens, and five Wimbledons spanning from 1994 through 1998, 2005, and 2007 through 2008, and 2009. She also won two US Opens in 1997 and 2000. She reached world number one in 2002 and held it for 11 weeks, with her peak years seeing her dominate alongside her sister Serena. Known for her powerful serve, consistently among the fastest in the sport, her exceptional athleticism, and her distinctive beaded hair braids and colorful on-court outfits, she transformed the women's game. She won fourteen Grand Slam titles in women's doubles, many with her sister Serena, making the Williams sisters a formidable force in doubles tennis. She competed in seven Olympic Games, a remarkable longevity record, and won multiple gold medals across singles and doubles events. She inspired a generation of players with her powerful game and presence, and her rivalry and partnership with Serena defined women's tennis.
